skill.name: swarm-orchestration
skill.description: Coordinate multi-agent workflows with agentic-flow. It covers swarm topologies, task orchestration, shared memory, hooks, load balancing, and recovery.
skill.summary: Coordinate agentic-flow swarms for parallel AI task execution, shared memory, and resilient workflow delivery.
skill.author: DNYoussef

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown fence or TypeScript example false positives, with no prompt injection evidence found. Two bash examples intentionally instruct users to run npx agentic-flow hooks, so they remain confirmed medium external command risks.

remediation.issue: Unpinned npx command examples execute a community CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the agentic-flow version and tell users to review package provenance before running commands.

remediation.issue: Hook commands process task descriptions and session identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Document what hook data is stored or transmitted, and warn users not to pass secrets.

remediation.issue: Command examples do not state when user approval is required.
remediation.suggestion: Add a safety note before bash blocks that commands should be reviewed before execution.

content.value_statement: Complex AI workflows become difficult when one agent must handle every task. This skill shows Claude, Codex, and Claude Code how to coordinate agentic-flow swarms across roles, topologies, and shared memory.
actual_capabilities: Explains mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive swarm topologies for agentic-flow workflows.
Shows quick-start hook commands for swarm initialization, agent spawning, and task orchestration.
Describes parallel, pipeline, and adaptive task execution patterns.
Covers shared memory patterns for cross-agent state coordination.
Outlines load balancing, retry, fallback, and performance monitoring options.
Provides troubleshooting guidance for coordination and performance issues.
limitations: Requires agentic-flow and Node.js 18 or newer.
Provides guidance and examples, not a complete swarm runtime implementation.
Examples assume the swarm API and hooks are available in the user environment.
External commands require review before use in sensitive projects.

use_cases.title: Plan Parallel Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Split implementation, testing, and review work across specialized agents with clear coordination rules.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Research Workflows
use_cases.description: Assign discovery, synthesis, validation, and reporting tasks to separate agents using shared memory.

use_cases.title: Design Resilient Agent Systems
use_cases.description: Choose topology, retry, fallback, and monitoring patterns for distributed AI workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Swarm
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a simple project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to plan a three-agent workflow for <project>. Include topology, agent roles, task order, and shared context.

prompt_templates.title: Split a Parallel Task
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate workflow planning for parallel execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to split <feature> across coder, tester, and reviewer agents. Include commands I should review before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Design Shared Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to define shared memory keys and handoff rules for <workflow>. Keep sensitive data out of shared memory.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize a Resilient Swarm
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced system design for large workflows.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use swarm-orchestration to design an adaptive swarm for <large project>. Include topology switching, load balancing, timeouts, retries, metrics, and recovery.

output_examples.input: Build and test a small REST API with three agents.
output: Recommended topology: mesh, because each role can coordinate directly.
Agent roles: coder, tester, and reviewer.
Execution plan: implement endpoints, write tests in parallel, then review the final result.

output_examples.input: Create a pipeline for design, implementation, testing, and review.
output: Recommended topology: hierarchical, with an architect coordinating ordered stages.
Pipeline stages: design first, implementation second, testing third, review last.
Shared memory should hold requirements, interface decisions, and test status.

output_examples.input: The swarm is slow and agents repeat work.
output: Check topology first and consider adaptive mode for uneven workloads.
Enable load balancing and monitor task queue length, latency, and agent utilization.
Use shared memory to prevent duplicate work and stale handoffs.

best_practices: Start with two or three agents, then increase size when coordination is stable.
Use shared memory for durable context, decisions, and handoff status.
Review every generated npx or hook command before execution.
anti_patterns: Launching many agents before task boundaries and ownership are clear.
Passing credentials, private data, or secrets through shared swarm memory.
Using adaptive orchestration without timeouts, metrics, or failure handling.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps plan and coordinate agentic-flow swarms for parallel tasks, pipelines, shared memory, and resilient execution.

faq.question: Does it run agentic-flow automatically?
faq.answer: It provides instructions and examples. Command execution depends on the host AI tool, available permissions, and user approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What prerequisites are needed?
faq.answer: The skill expects agentic-flow version 1.5.11 or newer and Node.js 18 or newer.

faq.question: Can it help choose a swarm topology?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains mesh, hierarchical, and adaptive topologies with common use cases for each.

faq.question: Is it safe for sensitive projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review external commands, avoid secrets in shared memory, and confirm what hooks store or transmit.
